title: May-minus-June warmth gave no clear repeated link to Meadow Brown flight dates in England and Wales, 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether the order of monthly warmth predicts Meadow Brown mean flight dates at a fixed May-June mean. We used 20,959 site-years at 1,320 public UKBMS sites in England and Wales in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. Four site-intercept models controlled time and August-September weather. Slopes for a 1 C warmer May and 1 C cooler June were +1.06, +3.43, +0.58 and +4.77 days. Only later Wales had a four-test adjusted interval above zero. All intervals included zero with year effects. Removing late-season controls kept all estimates positive, but early Wales changed sign after one year omission. The evidence does not establish a repeated nonzero link. Coarse weather, only 20 years per model, shared regional weather, selected sites and missing visit records limit inference. These are associations, not causal effects or climate-change attribution. The package includes code, source hashes, a figure, aggregate model moments and numerical checks. External record data stay outside the publication.

display.caption: May-minus-June temperature slopes at a fixed two-month mean in four site-intercept models. Lines show four-test adjusted intervals. Only later Wales excludes zero; all intervals include zero with year effects. Full UKBMS source attribution is in README.md and files/EXTERNAL_DATA.txt.

citations.reason: Prior Meadow Brown flight-spread study shares the biological archive. This study tests monthly temperature order against mean flight dates; it is not independent validation.
